summary: Wire the debug adapter of a csolution target and verify Load & Debug
triggers: a new target has no debugger yet
cmsis_action says a CMSIS task is not offered
unmapped: debug probe on the board or on the desk
flash algorithm for the internal flash in the cbuild-run file
verification: Check the cbuild-run file: its `debugger:` block names the adapter.

Check `.vscode/launch.json`: a configuration of `"type": "gdbtarget"` named after the adapter, such as `CMSIS_DAP@pyOCD (launch)`, `STLink@pyOCD (launch)` or `JLink (launch)`, and `.vscode/tasks.json` with the `CMSIS Load` task.
`serial_list_ports`: the probe's virtual COM port is a sign that the board is connected. `serial_open` it before anything runs, so that no output is lost.
`add_breakpoint` at the entry of the application code, not only at `main`.
`cmsis_action { action: 'load_and_debug' }`. Never `start_debugging` for a CMSIS target: it skips the flash download.
`continue_execution` and `wait_for_stop` to the breakpoint; `get_call_stack`, `get_variables_values` and one `read_peripheral_register` to show that stepping and reads work.
`remove_breakpoint` for the breakpoint you set, let it run, and `serial_read` the application's output.
stop_conditions: If the internal flash has no algorithm in the cbuild-run file, programming cannot work whatever the adapter is. Report that first.
Ask the user which probe is on the board or on the desk.
With several probes connected, the probe is chosen by the setting `cmsis-csolution.probe-id`, not in the csolution. Ask the user to set it.
When the files did not change: ask the user to open **Manage Solution Settings** in the CMSIS view and to confirm the debugger there, or to check that `cmsis-csolution.autoDebugLaunch` is on.
A launch configuration whose `cmsis` node says `"updateConfiguration": "manual"` is never rewritten; leave it alone and tell the user.
Ask the user to connect the board.
Read the hint of the failed result and `get_recent_problems` (`sources: ['gdb-server']`, `minSeverity: 'info'` shows what pyOCD or J-Link said), then continue with `$debugger-troubleshooting`.

extracted.title: CMSIS debug adapter name for each probe
extracted.body:
| Probe | Adapter name |
|---|---|
| CMSIS-DAP, DAPLink, on-board CMSIS-DAP | `CMSIS-DAP@pyOCD` |
| ST-Link, on-board ST-Link | `ST-Link@pyOCD` |
| ULINKplus | `ULINKplus@pyOCD` |
| MCU-Link, Nu-Link, KitProg3, PICkit, Raspberry Pi Debug Probe | `MCU-Link@pyOCD`, `Nu-Link@pyOCD`, `KitProg3@pyOCD`, `PICkit@pyOCD`, `RPiDebugProbe@pyOCD` |
| SEGGER J-Link | `J-Link Server` |

Use a name exactly as `csolution list debuggers` prints it.

extracted.title: Load runs the firmware before the debugger attaches
extracted.body: **Load runs the firmware before the debugger attaches.** In `load_and_debug` the pre-launch `CMSIS Load` task programs and starts the image; the session then restarts it and halts at `main`. A complete run's output can already be in the serial buffer at the first stop. Do not count that run twice.

extracted.title: At -Og a readback can show the old value right after a store
extracted.body: **At `-Og` the line table can be one volatile store early.** Right after stepping past a store, a readback may still show the old value. Let the code run on and read again before you suspect the hardware.

extracted.title: Diagnose a silent UART
extracted.body: **A silent UART**: halt, and read the UART's status, control and baud-rate registers with `read_peripheral_register`. A status register at its reset value means the peripheral is alive and its configuration is wrong; all zeros, or the same value in every register, means its clock was never enabled.

extracted.title: When the CMSIS Solution extension rewrites launch.json and tasks.json
extracted.body:
The CMSIS Solution extension rewrites both files when the csolution changes, as long as its setting `cmsis-csolution.autoDebugLaunch` is on (the default). Do not write them by hand.
A launch configuration whose `cmsis` node says `"updateConfiguration": "manual"` is never rewritten; leave it alone and tell the user.
